deletedSymbolAudit.incidentalFix: the repo's own manifest test was already failing after 1.0.12, and nobody noticed: it asserted the pre-1.0.12 exact-version peer whitelist, so replacing those whitelists with "*" turned it red. Original assertion: the test collected every declared @deepseek-ai/* peer range and asserted it equalled the old per-version whitelist string (the assertion that used to sit near test/client.test.mjs:397, i.e. 'manifest declares the exact supported DSH peer versions'). Why it went red: the whitelist strings no longer exist in package.json, so the comparison could not hold. What it asserts now: engines.dsh === ">=0.1.2-alpha.1", exactly one distinct DSH peer range and that it is "*", dsh.compatibility.dsh === ">=0.1.2-alpha.1", dshReleases entries for 0.2.0-rc.2 and 0.2.1-alpha.1 are "compatible", no declared specifier (peers + meta + dependencies + dsh.client.inject) names dsh-client-runtime or dsh-invariants, devDependencies still resolve to ["0.2.0-rc.2"], and peerDependenciesMeta["@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-store"].optional === true. Lesson for every fork in this batch: changing peerDependencies invalidates the upstream repo's own manifest assertions, so re-run the repo's test suite, not just the install gate.
